Spirited block rules for lighting levels
The aim of this section is to explain the standard that applies

Companion Animal Travel Desk Lighting and Crate Handling Standard

Staff must keep the desk area bright enough to read labels, inspect crates, and spot signs of distress without delay. The senior coordinator sets the daily check for lamps, shaded corners, and backup lighting, and any fault must be reported at once. <<FACT F068>> Small dog bookings are handled with the same care as larger animals, and the crate chosen must match the approved fit check before acceptance.

Before departure, staff must review the travel file, confirm the health papers, and give clear guidance to the passenger on feeding, water, and settling the animal. <<FACT F082>> If the document is out of date, or if the carrier shows signs of strain, the animal must not be cleared until the issue is resolved. Luna, if presented at the desk, must be treated under the same checks as any other pet, with steady handling and calm transfer between staff.

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps service dependable by using plain language, careful inspection, and prompt escalation when a risk appears. Any uncertain case, damaged crate, or passenger dispute must go to the senior coordinator before the animal is accepted for travel. Contact the senior coordinator for immediate review of any doubtful case.
